texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 01.08.2019 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. As per the facts of the case, on 21.02.2019, at about 07.30 AM, injured was going to attend a Barat by bus/ vehicle bearing no. DL 1PC 8959 and when he reached at M.B. Road, Ravi Das Marg, Majidia Hospital, T-Point, driver / R-1 asked the victim to remove the jam. On his request, he de-boarded the bus along with some other persons to remove the jam and after removing the same, when he was boarding the bus, the driver of the bus driven the bus suddenly in rash and negligent manner due to which, the victim fell down on the road and received grievous injuries. 3. Victim was taken to Safdarjung Hospital and medically examined and MLC was prepared. 4. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 338 IPC filed against the R-1. Further, present DAR also filed. 5. Further, R-1 & 2 filed their reply and it is stated that the police has registered false case against them. Further, the accident occurred due to the negligence of injured himself as he went down from the bus because of a rush on the road to clear the traffic which was not in the knowledge of the R-1 and when MACT No.: 630/19 Om Prakash Vs. Dharmender & Ors. Page No. 2 of 23 the traffic got cleared, the petitioner suddenly climbed up the running bus without the knowledge of driver and due to such negligence of him, he sustained injuries. Thus, presence of offending vehicle and that such offending bus was being driven by R-1 not denied but rash and negligent driving on the part of driver is denied. 6. Further, as per record, no reply filed by insurance company despite opportunity given. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal on 26.10.2021: 1. As per record, injured Om Prakash examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/6 relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. Further, as per record, none of the respondent led any evidence. 14. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 16. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1, it is noted that PW-1/Victim/Injured deposed on the lines of claimant's original stand, which is already noted above. PW-1 further deposed that due to such accident, he was treated in Sufdarjung Hospital and copy of medical report and OPD is Ex.PW1/3 (colly) and discharge summary as ExPW1/2. He further states that disability certificate Ex.PW1/6 (OSR) issued by concerned hospital Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, New Delhi in which total permanent physical impairment in relating to left lower limb is opined as 53%. 29.

Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as Om Prakash vs . The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full MACT No.: 630/19 Om Prakash Vs. Dharmender & Ors. Page No. 7 of 23 life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 24. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 24.1. 24.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that MACT No.: 630/19 Om Prakash Vs. Dharmender & Ors. Page No. 8 of 23 compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 24.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 24.4. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 24.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 24.7. 30. It is further argued on behalf of claimant / injured that due to such accident, he was not able to join his job for long time and still he is unable to work. 31. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is a vagueness in the claim that he is unable to work since the accident and no supporting documents/ witness proved in this regard. It is stated that as such, only a reasonable period for loss of income be granted, if so at all. 32. In the present case, it is claimed by the petitioner that he was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month from self employment of selling eggs but no supporting documents is filed nor so much expected by this Tribunal, But under these circumstances, his income is presumed based on minimum wages, prevailing in Delhi for unskilled worker at the time of accident. 33. Minimum wages for a unskilled worker at the time of accident on 21.02.2019 in Delhi was Rs. 14,000/- per month. Accordingly, it is presumed and held that petitioner was earning at least Rs. 14,000/- per month at the time of accident. It is further argued by petitioner side that accordingly functional disability of at least of 53% in relation to whole body be taken in the present case, as he was doing work of selling eggs and same do require constant standing and moving around for long hours each day. 36. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel or insurance company that there is no functional disability of 53 % in any case, in the present case. It is further argued that functional disability, if any is much lower as it physical disability is only one leg. As such, it is stated that at most, functional disability be calculated at 50% of the 53% physical disability in left lower limb in the facts and Om Prakash vs . Dharmender & Ors.
